## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-19T14:40:33Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: 72fb363e-dd25-4de3-9323-ca0cdee992ec
**Question**: - Q1: Only ready novelty-analysis results are exportable, read through U4's export read at their exact identity and hash, with eligibility re-checked. Research answers and discussions are not exportable.\n- Q2: You paste a Notion internal-integration token once (write-only). DocSuri lists the pages it can write to, you pick a parent page per export (last used preselected), and each export creates one new child page. Replacing the token or disconnecting invalidates pending approvals.\n- Q3: One "승인하고 내보내기" button records an approval bound to the result identity, hash and eligibility, the destination, the connection revision and the rendered-content hash, then starts exactly one export. Retries never start a second export. Any bound change, a revoked session or an expired result invalidates the approval.\n- Q4: Each page carries a DocSuri marker. Definite refusals end as failed. A rate limit retries within a small budget. Uncertain responses end as unknown and are never re-written automatically. A listing of the destination's children settles them (marker found means sent; a complete listing without it means failed). You can settle a lasting unknown from history.\n- Q5: Withdrawal deletes the token, cancels pending work and lets an in-flight export finish. Erasure deletes all export data and records evidence. Pages in your Notion are never touched.\n- Q6: A local fake Notion serves all tests. One real export to your own Notion test page follows, after you approve the exact content.\n- Q7: No usage-plan metering. One export in flight per owner, plus a per-owner pace limit.\n- Q8: An "내보내기" nav entry holds connection setup and export history. "Notion으로 내보내기" on the novelty result opens the stepped flow. It has five screen states, Korean labels, keyboard access and a live region. Unknown shows "확인 중", and success links the page.\n\nDoes this all look correct before I generate the artifact?
**Reply**: Looks correct

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-19T16:35:33Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: 72fb363e-dd25-4de3-9323-ca0cdee992ec
**Question**: - Q1: U6's own versioned key file seals each token, owner-only, outside the repository and database. It uses authenticated encryption bound to account and connection. Rotation re-seals tokens; a lost key means you reconnect.\n- Q2: The one real test export goes to your own single-member Free workspace. Its plan and the check date are recorded as free-terms evidence first.\n- Q3: Operating values:\n  - write timeout 90 s; settling wait 3 min\n  - checks over 24 h, then you are asked\n  - up to 3 rate-limit retries within 10 min\n  - an unreachable check waits 24 h, or 10 min during a retry\n  - orphan detection 15 min; clock margin 5 min\n  - 1 export at a time, 20 per hour; unapproved previews kept 7 days\n- Q4/Q5: The community Python SDK `notion-client` 3.1.0 runs inside the backend. U6 overrides its defaults:\n  - API version 2026-03-11\n  - automatic retries off, silent logging\n  - a 90 s timeout through an injected client limited to api.notion.com, verified TLS and no redirects\n  - manual pagination, and 529 read from the status\n  - errors reduced to fixed categories, with their token-carrying request chain never passed on\n\nDoes this all look correct before I generate the artifact?
**Reply**: Looks correct

**Session**: 72fb363e-dd25-4de3-9323-ca0cdee992ec
**Question**: Which notes from this stage should be kept for next time? (3 of 5)
**Reply**: [unit u8-service-operations-integration] Backup sets no longer carry key material: U6's security design keeps export keys out of every dump with no recovery copy, so a restore leaves the key folders untouched and each owner's own loss rule applies (U6 reconnect, U2 key recovery, an AccountAccess verifier replacement that ends every session). The first draft paired keys with their database, which the review showed contradicts U6., [unit u8-service-operations-integration] Dry runs and the soak use a disposable rehearsal copy, and the final run starts from an empty production database

## Question Replied

**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED

**Reply**: [unit u8-service-operations-integration] Backup and restore run as named platform operations under the separate operator authority (C10), with ServiceOperations only recording requests and evidence, [unit u8-service-operations-integration] The switch gains a maintainer-only window: the tunnel moves to v2 while only the administrator can sign in, so real Google and ORCID callbacks and each outward provider's first approved effect are exercised before anyone else arrives

**Unit**: u8-service-operations-integration

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-21T04:39:49Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: 72fb363e-dd25-4de3-9323-ca0cdee992ec
**Question**: U8's design passed its second independent look. All nine earlier concerns are fixed except a one-line leftover, and five points are still open: one Major (while a dry-run copy of v1's data is being made, or after a copy fails, the partial copy has no record and no disposal date) and four Minor consistency gaps (decisions not unfreezing after a late abort, a clash between incident rules, the final run's first two steps ordered differently in two places, and provider approvals not cleared after an abort). The design is now frozen, so fixing them means reopening it once more. Fix them now and re-check, or carry them to U8's approval and move on?
**Reply**: Fix them now and re-check (Recommended)

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-21T09:38:53Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: 72fb363e-dd25-4de3-9323-ca0cdee992ec
**Question**: Q14: You chose an external secured volume for backups. This Mac already has one: DocSuri_Backup, an encrypted volume on the external 2 TB SSD (731 GiB free), set up for REM-1 with its own backup account and an archive tool that checks every copy. Using it changes three rules in U8's design (backups currently live in the profile root), so the design is reopened for those rules first. How should backup sets be written there?
**Reply**: Through the REM-1 backup account (Recommended)

---

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-21T09:38:53Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: 72fb363e-dd25-4de3-9323-ca0cdee992ec
**Question**: Q15: The backups on DocSuri_Backup are protected by that volume's own encryption password. If this Mac dies, the drive can be read on another Mac only with that password. Is the password kept outside this Mac?
**Reply**: Password also kept off this Mac (Recommended)

---

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-21T09:38:53Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: 72fb363e-dd25-4de3-9323-ca0cdee992ec
**Question**: Q16: Q1's recovery time assumed auto-login, but FileVault is now on and auto-login is off. After a power cut the Mac waits at the unlock screen and nothing starts until you unlock it. How should recovery work?
**Reply**: Keep FileVault on (Recommended)

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-21T10:14:52Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: 72fb363e-dd25-4de3-9323-ca0cdee992ec
**Question**: The second check of U8's backup design closed all seven earlier gaps but found five new ones, three serious: (1) the archive is built in a folder only the service account can read, yet the separate backup account must read it to copy it to the drive; (2) the backup account deletes whatever a record says has expired, and the application can write those records, so a corrupted or forged record could delete a live backup, which undoes the reason for the separate account; (3) nothing keeps the last good backup and ledger copy, so if backups stop for a full retention period (drive left locked) those get deleted too. The smaller two: where the old tool's age-based cleanup marker sits on the drive is not stated, and the rollback rules and state table disagree on what happens before the rollback copy, with no way out if the drive is lost for good. Fix them now and get one more review, or carry them forward to U8's checkpoint?
**Reply**: Fix them now and re-check (Recommended)

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-21T11:05:53Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: 72fb363e-dd25-4de3-9323-ca0cdee992ec
**Question**: Concern (2) depends on which macOS account runs v2. You chose launch agents under your own login account, as v1 runs today. Any program running as your account can do whatever the operator tool can without a password. That includes running a backup check that restores an old backup, still holding deleted users' data, into a database it can read. Should v2 get its own account?
**Reply**: v2 on its own account (Recommended)

---

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-21T11:05:53Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: 72fb363e-dd25-4de3-9323-ca0cdee992ec
**Question**: The third review closed all five earlier gaps but found six new ones in U8's backup design, three serious: (1) the profile names a 'current' rehearsal database that nothing ever updates, so old rehearsal databases and their backups can never be deleted; (2) the account that calls the backup agent is never named, and if it is the same account the app runs as, the app could have backups read back; (3) the agent trusts the caller for a new copy's first disposal date and kind, so a wrong record could get the only copy of v2's database deleted early. The smaller three: a rollback copy that fails for reasons other than the drive has no defined path, a production restore may drop the last-good-backup protection, and nothing says how a replacement drive is set up. Fix them now, or carry them forward to U8's checkpoint?
**Reply**: Fix them now (Recommended)

---

**Options**: A. Exclude v2's folders and OrbStack's data (Recommended),B. Turn Time Machine's automatic backups off

**Question**: If the operations ledger itself is damaged, the incident the design asks for can't be written, because incidents are stored in that same ledger. How should this work?
**Reply**: Record it after repair (Recommended)

---

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-22T09:35:56Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: a97afe1b-0fe4-4f11-8e13-592e65e5a0ec
**Question**: U2's lifecycle worker always takes the oldest unfinished account request first, and U8's backups part of an erase can wait up to 24 hours for its restore check. If the worker keeps trying, that part uses up its 3 attempts in under a minute and the erase never finishes. If the worker waits instead, that one request blocks every request behind it. How should this be fixed?
**Reply**: Skip waiting requests (Recommended)

---

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-22T09:35:56Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: a97afe1b-0fe4-4f11-8e13-592e65e5a0ec
**Question**: When an owner erases their account, their status page would say the backups part is "erased" while backups still hold their data until each backup is disposed of. The design says the owner should see that date as "retained by policy", but the contract has no reason code or date for it. How should this be handled?
**Reply**: Add the reason and date (Recommended)

**Question**: The design says a member's session lasts 12 hours (an administrator's 1 hour), but the routers that set the session cookie end it in the browser after about 15 minutes. How should the cookie's lifetime be fixed?
**Reply**: Change the two routers (Recommended)

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-22T10:41:18Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: a97afe1b-0fe4-4f11-8e13-592e65e5a0ec
**Question**: The first sign-in of a migrated account needs three more changes in those same routers: the sign-in answer must carry the contract's consent-pending and reset-required results; the consent pages must accept a consent-pending session; and a migrated administrator without a second factor (today refused outright) needs a way to set one up. How should the administrator's case work?
**Reply**: Setup-only session (Recommended)

**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: a97afe1b-0fe4-4f11-8e13-592e65e5a0ec
**Question**: A migrated account that signs in only with Google or ORCID (no password) can't finish its first sign-in. The contract's identity sign-in answer has no "consents pending" result, so the provider path refuses it instead of opening the consent-only session that the password path gives. How should this work?
**Reply**: Add the consent result (Recommended)

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-22T12:44:34Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: a97afe1b-0fe4-4f11-8e13-592e65e5a0ec
**Question**: The design says U5's digest and U6's export limits lift only in live production. In code they can't lift there: digests go to exactly one permitted recipient and stop after 100 sends for the database's whole life, and the export needs its single test destination. Lifting them needs `u5_policy.py`, `u6_policy.py`, and U5's `delivery.py` and `scheduler.py`, which aren't on the plan's list. How should this be handled?
**Reply**: Lift them in live production (Recommended)

**Reply**: Cap per address, raise site cap (Recommended)

But installing a release with `docsuri-release install` while rolled back starts v2's three roles at its own `start` step, on the rollback's empty rehearsal database. Should install keep v2 stopped in that case?
**Reply**: Keep v2 stopped (Recommended)

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-25T06:25:07Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: a97afe1b-0fe4-4f11-8e13-592e65e5a0ec
**Question**: The review showed three holes in the per-address cap for Google/ORCID sign-in starts. A refused sign-in (for example, a Google account not yet linked) holds its place for 5 minutes, so three tries lock out everyone on that network. Nothing limits how often a start can be repeated, so one address can make DocSuri send Google or ORCID an endless stream of token requests. And one IPv6 range or one signed-in member can still fill all 200 places. How should U8 limit provider sign-in starts?
**Reply**: Count every start, free places at once (Recommended)

**Question**: The contract text written to match the code now says the scheduler's routine grant can run a production restore, which conflicts with the approved rules (BR4.7: a production restore runs only with the operator in person). The code doesn't refuse a scheduler production restore early either; it only fails later inside the driver. What should hold?
**Reply**: Production restore only in person (Recommended)

---

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-25T14:36:43Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: a97afe1b-0fe4-4f11-8e13-592e65e5a0ec
**Question**: The final verification run's journey J09 needs 20 GiB free after its database, but the Mac had about 14 GiB free during the run, even after every archived test copy was cleared and Colima's disk trimmed (swap holds 8 GiB). How should the room be made for the last run?
**Reply**: I'll free about 10 GiB more (Recommended)

---

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-25T14:36:43Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: a97afe1b-0fe4-4f11-8e13-592e65e5a0ec
**Question**: The installer's "stop v2 in person" step, and the keyring start, stop v2's three jobs with the fixed stop program directly, outside PlatformControl. That breaks the approved design (Workflow 20 step 9, BR6.12): each stop record should cite a receipt PlatformControl holds. It also leaves a gap: after a rollback, v2 is kept stopped, but stop records expire after 14 days, and no command can renew them. So a rollback left more than 14 days without a new dry run would lock up. How should stops work?
**Reply**: Add an in-person stop command (Recommended)

**Question**: When a Google/ORCID sign-in start is refused, the sign-in panel always says "같은 네트워크에서 진행 중인 Google·ORCID 로그인이 많아요" ("many sign-ins in progress on your network"), even when the whole site is busy or two starts collided. **Reply**: Different text for site-wide (Recommended)

**Question**: U8's code plan now has 382 tasks, 360 of them done. The new part is Step 44's box for your five decisions of 2026-10-25 after the final review, with its 8 test items (plan lines 2634–2653):\n\n- **In-person service control.** The operator tool gets `service stop <label>` and `service start <label>`, run in person. Each records its receipt before the stop record is written. The installer's stop item and its keyring start both use these commands. Running `stop` again renews a stop while a rollback keeps v2 stopped, and `cutover status` shows when each stop expires.\n- **Production restore only in person.** A standing (scheduled) production restore is refused with `production-restore-in-person` before any receipt is recorded. The scheduler's grant covers scratch restores only.\n- **Separate busy wording for the whole site.** Each sign-in refusal carries its reason, and the entry panel picks the network text or the site-wide text from it.\n- **Probe at soak start.** A release installed while v2 is stopped is recorded as not yet probed. When the soak starts, its probe runs, and if the probe fails the release is switched back and no soak starts.\n- **No soak until ready.** Kept as built.\n\nAfter that come the full verification and its final run, the code summary, and U8's review. Approve the plan?
**Reply**: Approve Plan

**Question**: A release installed while v2 is kept stopped is probed when the soak starts. If that probe fails, it's switched back to the previous release. As built, the switch-back then starts v2 on the previous release while the cutover record stays rolled back, so v2 runs without a soak. Either way, I'll make the start command safe to repeat on a job that's already running (today that wedges the switch-back). What should v2 do after a failed probe?
**Reply**: Leave v2 stopped (Recommended)

**Reply**: Give restore its own grant (Recommended)

Earlier runs' effects are settled before a new run starts.\n- **A stop for you:** if the operations tests pass their 300 s bound (they took 270.7 s), the build stops and asks you; the bound isn't raised.\n\nThen another adversarial review, the full verification with the final run and performance, and the code summary. **Question**: After a cutover rollback, the backup copies of the removed rehearsal databases are disposed of later. The new automatic retry in the scheduled (unattended) pass can't work in production, because disposal by event is an in-person agent word and the scheduler has no password. Which way?

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-26T08:40:53Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED

**Question**: In production, `docsuri-release install` runs as root, and its backup after writes stop calls the backup agent. The agent refuses root by design: root may only write the agent's first configuration. So every real install would fail at its backup step. How should the release command reach the agent?
**Reply**: Through your login (Recommended)

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-26T08:40:53Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: a97afe1b-0fe4-4f11-8e13-592e65e5a0ec
**Question**: In the platform store, each of production's three logins (operator, scheduler, the service's reader) can name any actor when it binds a receipt, because the store checks only the name it's given. So the scheduler could bind a receipt in your name. Receipts are evidence, not effects: effects still need sudo in person. But the isolation check and the ledger's decisions trust them. How should this be closed?
**Reply**: Bind each login to its actor (Recommended)

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-26T08:44:45Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: a97afe1b-0fe4-4f11-8e13-592e65e5a0ec
**Question**: U8's plan has a new box, "Your decisions of 2026-10-26 after the second review", plus two wording fixes:\n\n- **Your four answers.** The release reaches the backup agent through your login (two more password prompts at install). Leftover backup copies are disposed of only in person; the scheduled pass just reports them. Each production login is bound to its own actor in U8's store amendment, the reader gets read functions only, and the ledger's decisions need your in-person grant. `verify` probes any linked release still waiting for its probe.\n- **The receipt tightening.** A stop record counts as planned only if its stop receipt was bound within a named window around the stop, so an old receipt can't back fresh dates. The earlier wording ("settled no later than") was unworkable.\n- **The second review's Minors that concern behaviour**, each fixed with a test. Among them: exit code 5 counts as "already loaded" only after `launchctl print` confirms it; the scheduler's disposal right is limited to the backup volume; earlier effects settle before a release record begins; the release lock is re-checked where `service`, the soak start and the left-set retry act; stored grants are checked against the code.\n- **Wording:** after a switch-back both links name the kept release until the next install, and that's now stated.\n\nThen another adversarial review of this box, the full verification with the final run and performance, and the re-tick. Approve the plan?
**Reply**: Approve Plan

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-26T14:33:32Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: a97afe1b-0fe4-4f11-8e13-592e65e5a0ec
**Question**: The final run needs about 10 GiB more free disk for J09. Swap (24 GB) is the main thing eating it, and swap only shrinks on a restart or when memory pressure drops. How do you want to free room before the rerun?
**Reply**: I'll restart the Mac (Recommended)

---

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-26T14:33:32Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: a97afe1b-0fe4-4f11-8e13-592e65e5a0ec
**Question**: As built, `docsuri-release verify` starts v2's three roles whenever no soak is running, even when nothing waits for a probe. That removes stops you made in person, for example during the backstop return to preparing. Should verify start v2 only when it has a probe to run?
**Reply**: Only for a pending probe (Recommended)

---

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-26T14:33:32Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: a97afe1b-0fe4-4f11-8e13-592e65e5a0ec
**Question**: Suppose you roll back to a release that is still waiting for its probe, and that probe fails. The switch-back then points the links at the release you just rolled back from, whose record is closed, and only a new tag gets you out. What should happen?
**Reply**: Stay put, v2 stopped (Recommended)

---

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-26T14:33:32Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: a97afe1b-0fe4-4f11-8e13-592e65e5a0ec
**Question**: When `service stop|start` or the soak's start re-checks that no release command is running, production reads a cached copy of the ledger, so an install that has just begun can be missed. Which check should it use?
**Reply**: Check the release run lock (Recommended)

---

## Human Turn
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-26T14:34:49Z
**Event**: HUMAN_TURN
**Session**: a97afe1b-0fe4-4f11-8e13-592e65e5a0ec
**Picked**: ["Keep the built way (Recommended)","Reuse the kept folder (Recommended)"]

---

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-26T14:34:49Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: a97afe1b-0fe4-4f11-8e13-592e65e5a0ec
**Question**: U8's plan says an interrupted `docsuri-release verify` leaves a state that `recover` completes. As built, verify instead undoes what it started, `recover` has nothing to do, and running `verify` again completes the job. Which do you want?
**Reply**: Keep the built way (Recommended)

---

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-26T14:34:49Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: a97afe1b-0fe4-4f11-8e13-592e65e5a0ec
**Question**: Installing a tag that `release-previous` already names moves that kept folder aside while it clones the tag again. If the Mac loses power or the install is killed mid-clone, the real kept release is left in a hidden folder that the next install deletes, and `rollback` could point production at the partial folder. Which way?
**Reply**: Reuse the kept folder (Recommended)

A v2 you stopped stays stopped.\n- **A failed probe stays put.** If the kept release's record is closed, the links stay on the failed release, v2 stays stopped, and `recover-required` is marked; the runbooks say what next.\n- **The release run lock.** `service`, the soak start and the left-set retry check it right before acting.\n- **An interrupted `verify`** keeps the built way: run `verify` again.\n- **Staging reuses the kept folder** when its identity and commit match, and never moves a linked folder. `rollback` refuses an unreadable kept folder.\n- **The third review's Minors,** each fixed with a test or recorded with its reason.\n- **The final run happens after your restart,** and J09's bound isn't lowered.\n\nApprove the plan? If you do, the next step is your restart: I'll start the build when you're back.
**Reply**: Approve Plan

## Change Request: U8 runner gains the expired-environment v1 stop
**Timestamp**: 2026-10-30T06:43:23Z
- **Request**: at the U6 checkpoint the person chose "Fix the U8 runner first" (option 2) when the recorded whole-application check could not run: its U8 test environment under /tmp is expired and still holds the v1 supervisor state, so archive-owned refused (the v1-down prep read a runtime profile through LocalProfile.load: synthetic retention expired), and setup cannot start while the run root exists.
- **Action taken**: added preservation_manifest() to scripts/verify_docsuri_u8.py and routed run_v1 v1-down through it (resource, key-folder and stopped-application checks kept; the memory preflight and frozen-lock check stay live-only); u8_synthetic_v1.run_identity gained allow_expired, used only by v1_down, keeping the root, realm and database custody checks. Tests added in test_u8_tool.py (2) and test_v1_environment.py (3); ruff clean; the four files suites pass 80 tests.
- **Impact**: four U8-owned files changed during the U6 checkpoint window; they must be listed in the U8 source manifest and reviewed with the U8 code-generation work. No U6-owned file changed and no U8 record file was touched; the U8 realm remains expired and untouched: the set-aside retry follows.
- **Artifacts affected**: scripts/verify_docsuri_u8.py, scripts/u8_synthetic_v1.py, tests/u8_service_operations_integration/operations/test_u8_tool.py, tests/u8_service_operations_integration/operations/test_v1_environment.py.

**Event**: DECISION_RECORDED
**Stage**: code-generation
**Decision**: U8 loop-back: once Resend is live, a signed-out reset, verification or reactivation request for a mailed address waits on the Resend send while an unknown address answers at once, so answer time reveals accounts, which U2 BR2.1 and SD2-01 rule out. Send from an outbox, pad to a fixed floor, or record as residual risk?
**Options**: Send from an outbox (Recommended),Pad to a fixed floor,Record as residual risk
**Unit**: u8-service-operations-integration

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-02T06:43:48Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: b36696ea-bc6e-4c23-a17d-25ab6b32b40d
**Question**: Once Resend is live, a signed-out reset, verification or reactivation request (and registration, once it opens) for an address with an account waits for the email to go out. That's usually a fraction of a second and up to 30 s, while an unknown address answers at once. So the answer time tells whether an address has an account, and its state. U2's design rules that out (BR2.1, SD2-01). What should U8 do?
**Reply**: Send from an outbox (Recommended)

---

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-08T08:51:37Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: b36696ea-bc6e-4c23-a17d-25ab6b32b40d
**Question**: Sign-up, password-reset, verification and reactivation emails will be sent just after the answer, by a mail sender inside the app. If Resend is down or refuses them, or the sender stops, 운영 already shows it. But if the sender keeps running while every send fails because of a fault inside the app itself, people are told an email is on its way, none arrives, 운영 shows nothing, and only the app's log records each failure. Should those failures be counted on 운영?
**Reply**: Count on background work (Recommended)
**Options**: ["Count on background work (Recommended)","Keep the log only"]

---

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-08T08:51:37Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: b36696ea-bc6e-4c23-a17d-25ab6b32b40d
**Question**: When an imported account that must reset its password signs in, DocSuri checks no password and emails that account a reset link on the spot, so anyone who knows the address can set it off. While Resend is slow or shown as down, each try holds a server thread for up to 30 seconds. Every try sends a new email that takes one of the day's 90 shared email places, and the ordinary 'forgot password' request does the same for any account's address. So someone who knows one address can use up the day's email for every user within minutes, digests included. What should change?
**Reply**: Check first and cap daily (Recommended)
**Options**: ["Check first and cap daily (Recommended)","Check first only","Keep as built"]

---

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-08T08:51:37Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: b36696ea-bc6e-4c23-a17d-25ab6b32b40d
**Question**: In the planned app, sign-up, password-reset, verification and reactivation requests answer before their email is sent, and a test proves that no answer waits for an email. A request for an existing account still writes a few extra database rows, so it may answer a few milliseconds later than one for an unknown address. The account security design you approved asks for these answer times to be tested, but nothing measures them, before or after installation. How should this be handled?
**Reply**: Accept as recorded (Recommended)
**Options**: ["Accept as recorded (Recommended)","Measure on local copy","Measure after installation"]

---

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-08T08:51:37Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: b36696ea-bc6e-4c23-a17d-25ab6b32b40d
**Question**: When the mail sender cannot send an email, the plan tries it again once a minute until its 5-minute link ends. That rescues emails caught by a short Resend outage or a 'wait' (429) answer. But it also re-sends emails Resend refused outright, such as an address it rejects or a key it does not accept, up to five times, though no retry can fix them, and each refused try adds to Resend's error figure on 운영. How should the sender treat failed sends?
**Reply**: End refusals after one try (Recommended)
**Options**: ["End refusals after one try (Recommended)","Retry every failure","One try for all"]

## Decision Recorded
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-08T14:11:37Z
**Event**: DECISION_RECORDED

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-09T02:49:17Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: b36696ea-bc6e-4c23-a17d-25ab6b32b40d
**Question**: U1's own test lane fails its repository and integration phases for reasons older than U8. U1's setup never adds the discovery column U3 introduced on 15 October, and the paper publication those tests read needs Ollama 0.40.2, which Homebrew replaced with 0.40.15 on 8 November. U1's component phase passed on Colima, and every U8 run in Step 46(h) passed. How should Steps 46(h) and 105(b) check U1's lane? (Putting Ollama 0.40.2 back would let the publication run, but it changes the build live v1 uses; pick Other if you want that.)
**Reply**: Fix column, accept publication (Recommended)
**Options**: ["Fix column, accept publication (Recommended)","Component phase only","Accept today's failures"]

## Question Answered
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-09T02:50:22Z
**Event**: QUESTION_ANSWERED
**Stage**: code-generation
**Details**: U1 lane: Fix column, accept publication (Recommended). U1 setup also adds the U3 discovery column (as the U2 runner does); all three U1 phases run, and only tests that need the published papers may fail, each for that reason, recorded as an open item for U1.

**Reply**: Stop the grant (Recommended)
**Options**: ["Stop the grant (Recommended)","Keep and record it"]

## Question Answered

**Event**: QUESTION_ANSWERED

Template: Stop the grant (Recommended): U8 runner stops granting CONNECT on docsuri_u8_template and the privilege pin is re-taken in the same change.
**Unit**: u8-service-operations-integration

## Decision Recorded
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-09T12:25:32Z
**Event**: DECISION_RECORDED
**Stage**: code-generation
**Decision**: Batch 2 review: after a Resend attempt times out or answers 5xx the send may still go out under the same Idempotency-Key. A 408 or 409 on the retry is read as a definite refusal under L1-73, so the allowance place is released and the outbox row ended. The U5 digest email reads 408 and 409 as unknown. Which reading should hold?
**Options**: A Treat 408 and 409 as unknown like a timeout or 5xx so the place is kept and the row retried (Recommended),B Keep L1-73 as built so the status alone decides
**Unit**: u8-service-operations-integration
**Question Id**: 9ccfe5db
**Question Type**: stage-question
**Question Chat**: b36696ea-bc6e-4c23-a17d-25ab6b32b40d
**Question Shows**: sha256:1c0a5b336e7189ee5edf9891a881d293bb702b52caa239163d89d5c6c79e6d67

---

## Decision Recorded
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-09T12:25:33Z
**Event**: DECISION_RECORDED
**Stage**: code-generation
**Decision**: Batch 2 review: an existence leak in first_sign_in login. A reset-required imported account refused by require_admitted or by the reset account checks counts no failed sign-in, so it never reaches the 15-minute email wait that an unknown address reaches after five tries. That tells whether an address is an imported v1 account during the maintainer-only window, and for unverified imported accounts at any time. Fix it in this loop-back?
**Options**: A Fix it now by counting a failed sign-in before those refusals with a component test (Recommended),B Record it for the U8 checkpoint and leave the code
**Unit**: u8-service-operations-integration
**Question Id**: 407913e5
**Question Type**: stage-question
**Question Chat**: b36696ea-bc6e-4c23-a17d-25ab6b32b40d
**Question Shows**: sha256:c105ecf6288364e732026ad3c1a5d09433045d3120ea503ea1d315e3f8875c3c

## Question Answered
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-09T12:26:33Z
**Event**: QUESTION_ANSWERED
**Stage**: code-generation
**Details**: Red tests: Fix them now (Recommended): build Step 85(j) and (l) before Step 55, a sender pass before each mail read, the empty_outbox check and the check-first forced reset test, then run integration-1 to -4 on a fresh realm so later batches keep them green. 408/409: Treat as unknown (Recommended): a 408 or 409 reads as unknown like a timeout or 5xx, as the U5 digest email reads it, so the place stays reserved and the row retries a minute later; every other refusal stays final under L1-73. Sign-in leak: Fix it now (Recommended): count a failed sign-in before the require_admitted refusal and the reset account checks refusal, with a component test of six tries on each.
**Unit**: u8-service-operations-integration
**Message Id**: e523c148

## Decision Recorded
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-10T07:44:18Z
**Event**: DECISION_RECORDED
**Stage**: code-generation
**Decision**: The root installer gives its installation log to the service account by path after closing it (os.chown follows links), in a folder that account owns. During an installer run, that account could swap in a link and have root give it any file, such as a system file. Fix it now: create the log relative to a folder descriptor opened without following links, with O_EXCL, and fchown the descriptor before closing; the Step 76(g) test then records an fchown, with new cases where a planted link is refused. Or record it for the checkpoint?
**Options**: A Fix it now (Recommended),B Record it for the checkpoint
**Unit**: u8-service-operations-integration
**Question Id**: 5d910d07
**Question Type**: stage-question
**Question Chat**: b36696ea-bc6e-4c23-a17d-25ab6b32b40d

## Decision Recorded
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-10T07:44:19Z
**Event**: DECISION_RECORDED
**Stage**: code-generation
**Decision**: When the maintenance server fails to write an answer after its 5-minute window closed, it counts the failure in the open window while the closed window keeps the original count, so one request shows in two lines. Where the closed window is still unwritten, the count will move exactly as the plan says. For a window whose line is already written: count the failure in the open window, or drop it?
**Options**: A Count it in the open window (Recommended),B Drop it
**Unit**: u8-service-operations-integration
**Question Id**: 84b2fe0b
**Question Type**: stage-question
**Question Chat**: b36696ea-bc6e-4c23-a17d-25ab6b32b40d

## Decision Recorded
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-10T07:44:19Z
**Event**: DECISION_RECORDED
**Stage**: code-generation
**Decision**: At a stop, the maintenance server writes its final counts before closing, but requests still being answered at that moment count after that write and are lost. Accept that narrow loss and record it, or have the server wait up to 5 seconds, under the 30 second launchd stop limit, for those answers before its final write?
**Options**: A Accept and record it (Recommended),B Wait for those answers
**Unit**: u8-service-operations-integration
**Question Id**: 5d5fde3a

**Question**: Security finding in the installer: the root installer gives its installation log to the service account by path after closing it, and os.chown follows links. **Question**: The maintenance server sometimes fails to write an answer just after that answer's 5-minute window closed. ## Decision Recorded
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-10T18:38:28Z
**Event**: DECISION_RECORDED
**Stage**: code-generation
**Decision**: Batch 7 review: production has no path to a first Notion connection. ExportService.configure checks a candidate token that carries no account, and the composition builds ProviderActivation without the connection_owner read its own docstring names, so the maintainer is refused in rehearsal and in the live maintainer-only window and Notion can never be approved; the Step 88(b) test worked around it. Wire the connection owner read from the U6 connection table into ProviderActivation, with its grant and privilege pin, or carry the configuring account on the candidate token?
**Options**: A Wire the owner read (Recommended),B Carry the account on the token
**Unit**: u8-service-operations-integration
**Question Id**: eca9b435
**Question Type**: stage-question

## Decision Recorded
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-10T18:38:28Z
**Event**: DECISION_RECORDED
**Stage**: code-generation
**Decision**: Batch 7 review: a new password that fails only the password policy, or a blacklisted one, raises an exception no route maps, so registration, password reset completion and password change answer a bare 500, which also counts in the host error rate and which anyone with an entry context can cause at reset completion. Answer it with its own refusal and a plain Korean line asking for a stronger password, mapped in U8 files by overriding the two inherited U2 service methods, or answer it like an over-long password (409) with the screens unchanged?
**Options**: A Say the password is too weak (Recommended),B Treat it like an over-long password
**Unit**: u8-service-operations-integration

## Decision Recorded

**Event**: DECISION_RECORDED
**Stage**: code-generation
**Decision**: Batch 7 re-review: the database account can write postgresql.auto.conf, which the server reads after postgresql.conf, and point hba_file at a trust file, while the isolation check still passes on the checked pg_hba.conf. Pin hba_file and ident_file, and the listen settings, on the root-owned launch job command line, which outranks every config file, and have the isolation check read the server effective hba_file; or render postgresql.auto.conf and check it like the other rendered files?
**Options**: A Pin them on the command line (Recommended),B Render and check auto.conf

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-10T21:36:31Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: b36696ea-bc6e-4c23-a17d-25ab6b32b40d
**Question**: Batch 7's review found that production has no way to make the first Notion connection. ExportService.configure checks a candidate token that carries no account, and the composition builds the provider gate without the connection-owner read its own docstring names. So the maintainer is refused in rehearsal and in the live maintainer-only window, and Notion can never be approved. Step 88(b)'s test worked around it. How should the gate learn who owns a pending connection?
**Reply**: Wire the owner read (Recommended)
**Options**: ["Wire the owner read (Recommended)","Carry the account on the token"]

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-10T21:36:31Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: b36696ea-bc6e-4c23-a17d-25ab6b32b40d
**Question**: A new password that fails only the password policy, or a blacklisted one, raises an exception no route handles. Registration, password-reset completion and password change then answer a bare 500. Those errors count in the host's error rate, and anyone with an entry context can trigger them at reset completion. What should the member get instead?
**Reply**: Say the password is too weak (Recommended)
**Options**: ["Say the password is too weak (Recommended)","Treat it like an over-long password"]

---

## Question Replied
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-10T21:36:31Z
**Event**: QUESTION_REPLIED
**Session**: b36696ea-bc6e-4c23-a17d-25ab6b32b40d
**Question**: The re-review found that the database account can write postgresql.auto.conf. The server reads that file after postgresql.conf, so the account could point hba_file at a 'trust' file while the isolation check still passes on the checked pg_hba.conf. Any local account could then sign in as any database role. How should that be closed?
**Reply**: Pin them on the command line (Recommended)
**Options**: ["Pin them on the command line (Recommended)","Render and check auto.conf"]

## Decision Recorded
**Timestamp**: 2026-11-17T15:32:40Z
**Event**: DECISION_RECORDED
**Stage**: build-and-test
**Decision**: Build and Test failed: 21 targets this stage owns are failing (6 Not Met, 15 Unverified), 17 browser-only targets are said at the gate, 110 targets wait on later stages, and 3 tests in ci.yml's platform-integrity and ops suites fail only under this stage's umask 077. Root cause: U5's, U6's and U8's generated tests and U6's lint set-up, and two U8 behaviours (digest lateness counted from preparation, and no search breaker); 3 order-of-work targets have no fix. Candidate fix: loop-back 3 to Code Generation for U5, U6 and U8 (U5: test volume and a defaults-marker test; U6: real faults instead of four unlisted store doubles, the watch-counts and hostile-text cases, and E,F,I,UP,B Ruff rules for its tests and scripts; U8: digest lateness from the scheduled time, which reverses L2-17, both asset routes in isolation.spec.ts, a search breaker, and the sudoers, require_auth and late-rollback tests) — estimated impact — effort: about 3 to 5 days of build work (5 to 8 with the optional Chromium checks for the browser-only targets), then three Units' Plan Approvals, reviews and checkpoints and a rerun of this stage of about 3 hours; financial cost: $0, all local except U8-S part 2's optional arxiv.org fetch; risk: moderate. Loop-backs used: 2/3. Even after every fix, the 110 later-stage targets keep this stage failing until those stages run. How would you like to proceed?

**Question**: [Release engineer] Q1 of 6. The earlier Units' test commands that no workflow runs.\n\nYou settled earlier that each Unit's own workflow and test phases (its lane) "stay as they are". This stage's last check asks whether CI enforces every test command Build and Test recorded. For four earlier Units it does not:\n- U1 (paper journey): its lane only collects the backend tests, and its browser journeys run in no workflow.\n- U7 (platform protocols): its lane runs the component tests only.\n- U3 (paper corpus): its lane skips the backend coverage pass.\n- U2 (account controls): its browser journeys run in no workflow.\n\nWhat a change touches: the workflow files of U1, U3 and U7 belong to no Unit of this work, so changing them reopens nothing. U2's workflow file and the lanes' set-up tools are claimed by U8, so changing those reopens U8: it is reviewed, verified and approved again, and Build and Test is likely run again (a fifth loop-back, past the bound of three again). More database phases in CI also bring the PostgreSQL start-up race there. U1's phases need its model runtime and two papers from arxiv.org, a decision you left open.\n\nWhich do you choose?
**Reply**: Keep the lanes (Recommended)
**Options**: ["Keep the lanes (Recommended)","Add U3 and U7 only","Add everything"]
**Recommended**: ["Keep the lanes"]

**Question**: [Maintainer] Q2 of 6. The fixed home-folder path in U8's design, code and plan.\n\nEarlier you chose "Summary now, plan later" for this Mac's home path in U8's records: the code summary was rewritten with ~, and the plan was to follow before any commit. What is left in the plan is of a different kind. Four lines hold the real path: three quote the fixed Time Machine exclusion path for OrbStack's data folder, and one passes the bare home folder to a test that must refuse it.\n\nThat path is U8's approved design, not a leftover. The security requirement and the security design set it as a fixed absolute path, the isolation check (written, not yet committed) holds it as a literal, and three test files assert it. Rewriting only the plan would make it disagree with the code it describes.\n\nNothing new would become public: the account name is the same as the repository owner's public GitHub name, and 22 files already committed on develop hold the same path. Editing U8's approved files reopens U8, and Build and Test is then likely run again.\n\nWhich do you choose?
**Reply**: Leave as designed (Recommended)
